column1: # The jobs of .github/workflows/check.yml and what each one means for a landing or a move (package T8a; tools/gate/github_rule.py).
# The names are exactly the ones `gh run view <id> --json jobs` gives, a matrix leg with its own name. A self-test
# (tools/gate/tests/github_rule_test.py) compares this table with the workflow file: a job renamed, added or removed there
# fails the tools check until this table follows.
#   must      a landing with the group `github-first` waits for it to be green before main moves (any push run of that commit, the

#             newest result wins); one with `github` alone reads it after the move (a red one opens a repair); a red one stops the run. A job this table does not name counts as must, and the run says so in a line of kind tool.
#   nightly   left out of every rule: this machine builds and tests Windows and Android itself (a landing whose plan has
#             the group `android` runs the Android build here; GitHub's two Android builds take about 50 minutes each).
#   advisory  never blocks: a red or cancelled one is run again once; red again, it is told in one line.
# A change whose scope (tools/gate/scope.tsv) has neither `github` nor `github-first` does not push a candidate and reads none of them.
# check.yml runs a nightly job only on main and by hand, not on a candidate (gate/**); a self-test (github_after_test.py) compares the classes with the jobs' conditions.
